- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Model overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., post-80.00+), often overshooting by 5–10% and failing to correct.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: after a spike, it incorrectly assumes prices will fall too quickly or too far.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the 30-day window.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of price corrections after a peak, especially in the final 5–10 days.
- Model is overly sensitive to recent low prices, leading to premature downward bias when prices are recovering.
- Model fails to capture the “tail” of price volatility — underestimates the final 5–10 days, especially when true prices show strong upward momentum.
